introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Copy and complete the table above. *[2 marks]*
(b) Show that the number of candidates for the years [range of years illegible in the printed paper] above forms an arithmetic progression. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A sequence is an arithmetic progression (A.P.) when the difference between consecutive terms is constant. For the six values $3750,\ 5000,\ 6250,\ 7500,\ 8750,\ 10000$:

$$5000-3750=6250-5000=7500-6250=8750-7500=10000-8750=1250.$$

The difference is the same ($1250$) every time, so the numbers of candidates form an A.P. with first term $a=3750$ and common difference $d=1250$. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Find the number of candidates who registered in the year 2021. *[3 marks]*
(d) Find the total number of candidates who registered from 2010 to 2021. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From 2010 to 2021 there are $n=12$ terms, with first term $a=3750$ and last term $l=17500$.

$$S_{12}=\frac{n}{2}(a+l)=\frac{12}{2}(3750+17500)=6\times21250=127\,500.$$

(Check with the other formula: $S_n=\frac n2[2a+(n-1)d]=6[7500+11(1250)]=6\times21250$ ✓.)

**The total number of candidates from 2010 to 2021 is $127\,500$.**
